outcome: Admission to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU)
cohort: Singleton, vaginally born infants at >=33 weeks of gestation who were either crying or non-crying but breathing within 30 seconds after birth.
finding: Non-crying but breathing infants immediately after birth had a higher risk of both bradycardia and tachycardia, and admission to the neonatal intensive care unit compared to crying infants.
